correctness.rationale: Eliminating the bottom labels gives y_i=x_{i+2} and x_i+x_{i+1}+x_{i+2}=0; subtracting consecutive relations gives period 3. If 3 divides n, both cap sums vanish for all seeds; otherwise the cyclic word is constant and 3w=nw=0 forces w=0 by Bézout, including in 3-torsion groups. The same elimination in the presented free abelian group proves the integral Smith claim, not only a rank claim. The nonzero count is (q−1)(q−2), and generativity is exactly generation by the first two entries; cyclic groups of order ≥3 or infinite cyclic admit the equal-generator pair. Strong pairs are precisely lifts of ordered distinct nonzero doubles in 2Γ[4]. Those two independent doubles imply the two lifts span a copy of (Z/4)^2 by reducing a prospective relation successively modulo two; if they generate all of Γ, it is that copy. In the interleaving the graph is C_{2n}²; for 2n≥8 the distance-one and distance-two edges lie in two and one triangles respectively. Thus its full automorphism group preserves the long cycle and is exactly dihedral. The induced action on the periodic positions is S₃. Its identity, transposition and 3-cycle fixed counts are (q−1)(q−2), q−|Γ[2]| and |Γ[3]|−1. Strong triples have no repetitions. This gives all stated orbit counts and in particular 210, 41, 96 and 16 for the indicated example.
